# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

EMPTY SEED. `prompt.md` was 0 bytes and there was no `task_template.md`, so the agent ran with **no
system message at all** (adapter `_read_system_prompt`: an existing-but-empty file means *send no
system turn*) and with the adapter's built-in `_TASK_TEMPLATE` as its only instruction. I created
both files from scratch. Baseline val 0.450 (18/40).

No ENVIRONMENT fault found. All 22 failures produced a file at the correct `output_path` and had
zero tracebacks and zero sandbox errors; every failure is a capability failure. Verified: for 9569
and 59196 the agent's `wb.save(...)` path is byte-identical to the prompt's `output_path`.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Formula string written into graded cells** | 37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942 (7) | Grader reads stored values with `data_only=True` and never recalculates. openpyxl writes no cached value, so an `=`-string reads back as `None`. Agent never knew this — grep for `recalc`/`data_only`/`cached` across all 7 traces: **0 hits**. The instruction says "formula" in 6/7, and the agent took the word literally. | KNOWLEDGE (missing fact) + CONTRACT | Add the sourced rule + tighten output contract (SKILL levers 4, 8) |
| 2 | **Never verifies its own output; burns the round cap re-sending identical code** | all 22, decisively 37456, 53647, 54144, 43436, 9569, 227-40, 55049, 6698, 7902, 46897 (10 hit the 30-round cap) | `[Code executed successfully with no output]` is read as success. **Zero** `print()` of the saved file in any of the 22 traces; `data_only=True` appears nowhere. Unique code blocks per 30-round trace: 2–4. The built-in template's line *"once that file exists, you are done"* actively licenses this. | BEHAVIORAL → needs STRUCTURE | Ordered 3-phase procedure with read-back as a precondition of stopping (SKILL levers 6, 1); DELETE the contradicted "you are done" line |
| 3 | **Excel error text / wrong type in graded cells** | 37456, 53647, 54144, 56563 (4) | Downstream of #1: the formula the agent wrote resolves to `#N/A`/`#NAME?` (54144 used Excel-365-only `TEXTSPLIT`), so the cell holds a `str` where an `int`/`float` was expected. | KNOWLEDGE + CONTRACT | Explicit type contract, incl. "an error marker is never an answer" |
| 4 | **Ambiguous instruction resolved by assertion when the file settles it** | 39046, 43436, 50768, 267-18, 55979, 51-12, 80-42 (7) | The disambiguator was in the file and unread: an already-filled worked example (39046: F2:F4 = `2,2,0` contradicts a grand total), a neighbouring formula (43436: `=COUNTIFS(B:B,G2,D:D,"")` names the grouping key), axis labels (50768: rows are Impact not Likelihood), the existing formula string (267-18), a blank-row boundary (80-42). | KNOWLEDGE (criterion for resolving ambiguity) | New rule + worked example of the reasoning (levers 4, 5) |
| 5 | **Destructive `to_excel` rebuild of a sheet whose rows must survive** | 80-42 (6489 pre-existing cells lost), 43436 (flattened H's formulas), 39046, 50768 | Rebuilt the sheet from a DataFrame instead of appending/setting cells. 80-42 was an append task and appended **zero** rows after a row-count coincidence convinced it the job was done. | KNOWLEDGE + DECISION (narrowed) | Additive rule stating the two conditions that *require* openpyxl — deliberately NOT a global ban (see blast radius) |
| 6 | **Preview mis-read → wrong rows, or extent guessed from the sample** | 59196 (off-by-one: read row 1 for headers that sit in row 2 → wrote `None`), 227-40 (`# Based on the provided snippet, rows 0,1,2 have data` → capped at 4 rows), 48527 | The preview is `read_excel().head()`; pandas ate Excel row 1 as the header and the index column is not column A. The `[data extent]` line is accurate but was ignored in favour of the printed sample. | KNOWLEDGE (format fact) | State the preview→Excel mapping precisely |
| 7 | **Float/blank arithmetic** | 51-12 (`110 >= 100*1.1` is False — count 2 vs 4), 48527, 50768 | Exact float comparison on percentage arithmetic; `NaN` treated as 0. | KNOWLEDGE | Named pitfall + the tolerance idiom |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Add a sourced rule (4) + role/goal line (7) | `prompt.md` §1(a) | States the grading mechanism (`data_only=True`, no recalc) and its consequence, plus the *reason* — so it extends to cases I never wrote down. Explicitly covers "even when the instruction says 'formula'". General: no task id, no value. | YES — 0/18 passing traces write a formula string (grep for `= "=…"`/`f"=`: 0 hits). 9 of them were asked for a "formula" and all 9 wrote literals. The rule is 18/18 already-compliant. |
| 1, 3 | Tighten the output contract (8) | `task_template.md` CONTRACT §1–2 | The contract restated as 4 numbered, checkable items at the point of use. Lever-8's default. | YES — describes what all 18 already do. |
| 3 | Add a sourced rule (4) | `prompt.md` §1(b) | Types must match; numbers never as formatted strings; dates as `datetime`; an error marker is never a computed answer — with what to do instead. Values verified against scorer `transform_value` / `_EXCEL_ERROR`. | YES — no passing trace writes a formatted-number string (`astype(str)`, `:,.2f`, `'$'`: 0 hits). |
| 1, 3 | Add a sourced rule (4) | `prompt.md` §1(c),(d) | 2-decimal rounding and `None`≡`""`, read off `transform_value` and `compare_cell_value`. Neither was discoverable. | YES — additive facts; no passing behaviour depends on not knowing them. |
| **2** | **Restructure into an ordered procedure (6) + delete contradicted text** | `task_template.md` HOW TO WORK | Three ordered phases. INSPECT is a precondition of WRITE; the read-back print is in the **same block** as `wb.save`, and Phase 3's checklist is the precondition of stopping. Stopping is redefined as *"reply with no code block"* — which is exactly how the adapter's loop breaks (`if solution_code: break`), so the instruction and the runtime agree. **Deleted** the built-in's "once that file exists, you are done", which contradicts every verification rule I added. | Analysed as the riskiest edit — see blast radius below. |
| 2 | Rewrite positively (1) | `task_template.md` Phase 3 | "Do not re-send working code — a resubmission changes nothing" replaces the implicit licence to idle. Aimed at the 2–4-unique-blocks-per-30-rounds pattern. | Cap cost is not a concern: 10 passing tasks already waste ~26 rounds on no-op resubmits. |
| 4 | Add a rule + an example (4, 5) | `prompt.md` §2 | Three named disambiguators — already-filled target cells, neighbouring/existing formulas, axis labels — plus one `<example>`-style worked reasoning chain showing how `2, 2, 0` refutes a grand total. Generic (`F2:F6`, values `2,2,0`) and matches how the *passing* 39046-class traces reason, not an answer. | YES — additive. 560-12 already reasons this way (`answer_position` vs instruction) and passes. |
| 4 | Add a sourced rule (4) | `prompt.md` §2, para 3 | Modify a formula by rewriting the expression, never by prepending text to the whole cell value. | YES — no passing trace edits a formula string. |
| **5** | Add a rule that NARROWS (4) | `prompt.md` §4 | States the **two discriminating conditions** that require openpyxl (an append/consolidate instruction; the sheet holds content the DataFrame does not carry), and explicitly blesses `to_excel` otherwise. Includes the first-blank-row idiom. | Deliberately narrowed — see blast radius. |
| 6 | Add a sourced rule (4) | `prompt.md` §3 | preview row `i` ⇒ Excel row `i+2`; the index column is not column A; `Unnamed: k` ⇒ column `k+1`; the `[data extent]` line is whole-sheet and authoritative while the printed rows are a sample. Read off adapter `_spreadsheet_preview`. | YES — 15/18 passing tasks use `read_excel`, which already sees the true extent; the facts only prevent the off-by-one. |
| 7 | Add a sourced rule (4) | `prompt.md` §5 | Float tolerance (`>= b - 1e-9`), blanks≠zeros, `NaN`→`None`, `dropna(how="all")` shifts rows. | YES — additive pitfalls; passing traces hit none of them. |
| 6 | Clarify the contract | `task_template.md` field list | `answer_position` **bounds where**, the instruction **says what** — "do not spread your answer over the whole range just because the range is bigger". | YES — and it *protects* 560-12, which wrote I3:J6 inside a I2:J7 target because the instruction said "from I3", and passed. |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change)
- **1 —** trace 37378: `formula = f'=IF(B{{row}}<>"", COUNTA($B$2:B{{row}}), "")'` → `ws[f'A{{row}}'] = formula`; the feedback confirms *"The formula logic itself was right"*. §1(a) says compute and assign the literal ⇒ the same correct logic evaluated in Python writes `1..5`. Same decisive line quoted in 46897/53383/6698/7902/8942. **55049 is the proof**: it had the right literals in `results` from `mapping.get(place, 0)`, wrote `# the user wants a formula`, and assigned the formula instead — §1(a) resolves exactly that deliberation the other way. Contract checked against the scorer, not the old prompt: `compare_workbooks` loads `data_only=True`, and `_matches` is called on the as-saved file (`REWARD_RECALC=0`, primary metric `hard_no_recalc`) — so a formula genuinely reads as `None`.
- **2 —** all 22 traces contain zero `print()` of the saved file and zero `data_only=True`; 46897 resubmitted one byte-identical block 28 times against `[Code executed successfully with no output]`. Phase 2 puts the read-back in the same block as `wb.save`, so the agent cannot reach Phase 3 without having printed what the grader will read; Phase 3's checks are the stated precondition of stopping. Structural, not restated: the old template had no verification step to skip.
- **3 —** trace 54144: `cell.value = f'=SUM(SUMIFS(Data!$D:$D, Data!$C:$C, TEXTSPLIT(C{{row}}, ", ")))'` on all of D3:D10 → 8/8 cells `#N/A`, `str` where `float` expected, and D3:D6 (the worked example) clobbered. §1(a)+§1(b)+§2 each independently block this; the Phase-3 error-marker check catches it if they don't. Marker list verified against adapter `_EXCEL_ERROR`.
- **4 —** trace 39046: `# This implies we might need to put the total in each cell or a running count. # Given the context … it's likely the total.` → `df['No. Subs'] = yes_count` wrote `4` five times; expected `[2,2,0,2,2]`, and F2:F4 already held `2,2,0`. My §2 example is that exact refutation pattern. 43436: never mentions the grouping key despite `=COUNTIFS(B:B,G2,D:D,"")` sitting in the neighbouring column — §2's "print the formulas of neighbouring columns" surfaces it. 50768: asserted `# Row 12 → Likelihood 3` without reading E12:E14 = `3,2,1` / F15:H15 = `1,2,3` — §2's axis-label rule.
- **5 —** trace 80-42: `elif len(target_df) == len(new_data_df): # It's already consolidated` → appended 0 of ~3998 rows, then `ExcelWriter` rewrote all four sheets and lost 6489 pre-existing cells. §4's append clause gives the first-blank-row scan (the passing approach found row 4000 this way) and forbids concluding from a row-count coincidence.
- **6 —** trace 59196: `headers = [ws['D1'].value, …]` read the empty Excel row 1 because the preview showed the headers in DataFrame row 0; every `headers[max_idx]` was `None`, so `ws[f'H{{row_num}}'] = None` wrote nothing into H3:H5. §3's `i ⇒ i+2` mapping is precisely this fault. 227-40: `# Based on the provided snippet, rows 0, 1, 2 have data` → `range(min(4, …))` → 5 cells empty; §3's "the printed rows are a sample; the extent line is authoritative".
- **7 —** trace 51-12: `if val >= ref_val * 1.1:` — I confirmed in Python that `110 >= 100*1.1` is `False`, so the first 10% step is missed (count 2, expected 4); the passing approach used `- 1e-9`. §5 states that idiom.
- **Template contract —** rendered the template with all seven placeholders: required set complete, no unknown keys, `str.format` succeeds, HTML comment stripped. Re-ran after every edit.

## Blast radius per edit
**BOUNDED (additive knowledge / contract clarification the 18 passing tasks already satisfy):**
prompt §1(a)(b)(c)(d), §2, §3, §5; template CONTRACT and field list. Evidence: across all 18 passing
traces, formula-string writes = 0, formatted-number-string writes = 0, error markers = 0,
preview-extent reliance = 0 (15/18 use `read_excel`, which reads the whole sheet). These rules
describe what the passing tasks already do, so they cannot flip an action.

**The two edits that DO change behaviour on passing tasks, and why each is safe:**

1. **prompt §4 (`to_excel` → openpyxl) — narrowed on purpose.** I enumerated the class first: **13 of
   18 passing tasks produce their output with `to_excel`/`ExcelWriter`** (12864, 142-12, 2768,
   31628, 382-10, 395-36, 402-43, 463-17, 47798, 48588, 48921, 59595, 9726). A global "always use
   openpyxl" rule would rewrite all 13 — and would outright **break** 395-36 and 402-43, whose
   target sheet does not exist in the input (`MyResult`, `Sheet2`), and 463-17 and 402-43, which
   must produce more rows than the source has. That is the UNBOUNDED decision-rule mistake the
   instructions warn about, so I did not write it. Instead §4 blesses both approaches and names
   only the two conditions under which openpyxl is required: an append/consolidate instruction, and
   a sheet holding content the DataFrame does not carry. Checked against the class: none of the 13
   is an append task, and each rebuilds a sheet it fully owns. 9726 writes J2:J19 for a 1-cell
   target — §4 permits that ("filling an empty helper cell is harmless"); only *destroying existing
   content* is forbidden, which 9726 does not do.
2. **template HOW TO WORK (3-phase procedure) — changes 18/18, since no task does read-back today.**
   Bounded three ways. (i) **Round budget:** 10 of the 18 already run the full 30-round cap
   re-sending identical code, so inspect + read-back rounds are free; the 1–3-round tasks have ≥27
   spare. (ii) **Revision risk:** four passing tasks are correct in their *first* block (12864,
   45635, 47798, 48588) and gain a look at their own output. Phase 3 is deliberately a **closed
   checklist of six falsifiable items** (no `=`-string, no error marker, no unexpected `None`,
   right type, unasked cells unchanged, reproduces the worked example) followed by "if every check
   passes, you are done — reply with no code block. Do not re-send working code." All four pass all
   six checks, so the procedure terminates them rather than inviting an open-ended rewrite. The
   one precedent for this agent revising a settled answer (560-12, block 9) stayed correct.
   (iii) **Stop mechanism matches the runtime:** "reply with no code block" is exactly the
   adapter's `if solution_code: break`, so a satisfied agent exits cleanly instead of idling.
   I also protected the two passing tasks whose *task is to change existing cells*: 382-10 (writing
   `None` over non-"comments" cells **is** the requested operation) and 560-12 (instruction beat
   `answer_position`) — hence "change **or clear**" in the preserve rule, the explicit "if the task
   *is* to clear cells, `None` is correct" carve-out in the Phase-3 checklist, and the field-list
   line that the instruction governs *what* while `answer_position` bounds *where*.

**Deletion:** one line removed — the built-in template's *"once that file exists, you are done"*.
It is not redundant, it is **contradicted**: it is the licence for cluster #2 (22/22 traces stop or
idle on an unverified file). Its only real constraint — "write the file to `output_path`" — survives
in the field list, the CONTRACT preamble, and Phase 2. No passing trace depends on the removed
clause; the 10 cap-hitting passing tasks demonstrate that it does not even stop them early.

## Process & features used
- **Subagents: yes, 4 read-only `Explore` agents in parallel** (2 + 2), one per trajectory group —
  formula cluster, `#N/A`+coverage clusters, wrong-value cluster, and one profiling all 18 **passing**
  traces against my five draft rules before I wrote them. That last one is what stopped me shipping
  the global `to_excel` ban (it found the 13-task blast radius and the two tasks it would break) and
  what surfaced the 382-10 clearing carve-out. I then merged all findings into this one candidate
  myself and re-validated the template after each edit.
- I also read the adapter and the vendored scorer directly to source every stated constant:
  `compare_workbooks`/`cell_level_compare` (values only, `data_only=True`), `transform_value`
  (2-decimal rounding, `""`≡`None`), `_EXCEL_ERROR` (the marker list), `_spreadsheet_preview` (the
  `i+2` mapping and the whole-sheet extent), `_read_system_prompt`/`_read_task_template`,
  `_TEMPLATE_REQUIRED`, and the rollout loop's break conditions. No number in either file is guessed.
- Prior iterations: **none exist** (`RUNMAP.md` empty, `LEDGER.md` baseline-only, `rejected.jsonl`
  absent). Nothing to build on or avoid; this iteration establishes the baseline others read.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- §1(a) "a formula is not an answer, even when the instruction says 'formula'" — the single largest
  cluster (7 tasks) and a fact the agent provably cannot derive.
- The read-back living in the **same code block** as `wb.save`. Split into a later round it becomes
  skippable, and 22/22 traces show this agent skips optional verification.
- The narrowed form of §4. Do **not** promote it to a global "never use `to_excel`" — that breaks
  395-36, 402-43 and 463-17 (target sheet absent / more rows than the source).
- "Reply with no code block" as the stop signal — it is the adapter's actual break condition.
- The "change **or clear**" phrasing and the clearing carve-out, which keep 382-10 safe.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- **Nothing was skipped for lack of effort** — every one of the 7 clusters above got an edit.
- **No environment-fault cluster existed** to hand back: 0 tracebacks, 0 sandbox errors, and every
  failing task wrote a file to the correct path. I checked specifically because 9569/59196 look like
  "wrote nothing" failures; they are not — 9569 wrote 1280 `IFERROR(…,"")` formulas (cluster 1) and
  59196 wrote 3 `None`s from an off-by-one (cluster 6).
- **Did not add per-task tactics** (VLOOKUP recipes, pivot idioms, matrix-orientation heuristics).
  Those would be task-specific and would not generalize; §2 instead gives the general method of
  reading the intent out of the file.
- **Did not touch** the adapter, scorer, harness, benchmark or `{placeholder}` contract. Only
  `prompt.md` (created) and `task_template.md` (created) changed.
